newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Foschini sees no improvement until H2.
newsitem.headline: Foschini sees no improvement until H2.

text.p: South African clothing retailer Foschini Ltd said on Wednesday it was approaching the new year with caution and it was unlikely that any earnings improvement would be seen until the second half of the financial year.

"A number of initiatives have been taken in an attempt to secure growth, but the macroeconomic environment will have a significant impact on the year as a whole," Foschini said in a statement accompanying year end results.
"It was unlikely that any improvement will be seen until the second half," it said.
Despite this the group continued to invest heavily in order to position itself for further growth when conditions allowed. Forty-five new stores would be opened in the 1997/98 year, it said.
Foschini recently acquired a sporting clothing and goods retailer, Sports Scene, and started a new jeans and casual wear business called RJL. It said these held "exciting opportunities".

Foschini earlier reported a sharp slide in year attributable earnings to 77.9 cents a share from 107.4 cents before. As is group policy, Foschini will award capitalisation shares to shareholders instead of a dividend.
